Definition: superlative of ἀκρίβης (a derivative of the same as G206); most exact:--most straitest.
BiblicalUsage: Once, before Agrippa: Paul says the Jews knew him from the beginning, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee. The word is the superlative — the strictest, the most exact.
TheologicalSignificance: One superlative in one verse carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Paul's point, that the strictest sect produced the greatest apostle of grace.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
